text:
Anya: Started 3% canary for v7-int4 on /generate with focus on long-context (>2500 tokens). Early diffs show lift in hallucination for that slice.
Ben: numbers?
Anya: quick readout:
```
long-context:
  baseline(v6-fp16): halluc_rate=3.5%, mrr=0.860
  v7-int4:          halluc_rate=6.0% (+2.5pp), mrr=0.849 (-0.011)
short:
  no material change
cpu savings ~22%
```
Rohit: That +2.5pp on long-context is above our 2pp guard. Are we using the same eval harness?
Anya: yes, identical harness and anchor set. Also saw kv-cache hit drop ~4.2pp for long prompts.
Clara: Sounds like cache churn from different kernel ordering for quant path. Proposal: immediately pin long-context traffic to baseline and reduce canary to 0.5% while we collect deterministic seeds.
RolloutBot: Canary 4967890123 started -> pool "dedicated-s" (A100). No runtime errors.
Ben: Also run v7-fp16 quick build to check if regressions persist without quantization.
Rohit: If fp16 matches baseline, then try per-layer mixed-quant: keep attention/query/proj in fp16 and rest int4. That often fixes cache-sensitive regressions.
Anya: Action: 1) throttle 3%->0.5% now; 2) pin long-context to v6; 3) seed-run 50k long-context queries; 4) start v7-fp16 build and mixed-quant sweep.
RolloutBot: Traffic changed at 4967890140: 3% -> 0.5%. Routing updated: long-context pinned to v6-fp16. Shadowing for v7-int4 continues.
Clara: I'll add an auto-fallback rule: long-context hallucation delta >= 2.0pp -> auto-reroute.
Ben: Thanks—please add MRR smoothing so we don't flip on noisy batches.
Anya: Will do. I'll post eval links when ready.
